subject: math
title: Mass and Liquid Volume
seo_title: Grade 3 Mass and Liquid Volume Worksheets: Grams, Kilograms, Liters, Scales and Word Problems
standard_text: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l). Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 mass and liquid volume worksheets: choose grams, kilograms or liters, estimate with benchmarks, read scales and containers, use a pan balance, and solve one-step word problems. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Grams and kilograms tell how heavy. Liters tell how much liquid.
key_sub: A paper clip is about 1 g, a dictionary about 1 kg, and a large water bottle about 1 L. On a scale, find what one mark is worth before you count.
body_html:
Mass and liquid volume

Mass tells how heavy something is. We measure it in grams (g) for light things and kilograms (kg) for heavy things. Liquid volume tells how much liquid a container holds. We measure it in liters. You may see liters written as l or L. Both mean liter. This page uses L.

Benchmarks: know what 1 unit feels like

Compare a new object with something you know. Then choose the unit and a sensible number.

UnitAbout the same asMore examples
1 gram (g)a paper clipa nickel is about 5 g, an apple about 150 g
1 kilogram (kg)a big dictionarya watermelon is about 5 kg, a bicycle about 15 kg
1 liter (L)a large water bottlea milk jug holds about 4 L, a bucket about 10 L

Read a scale

Not every mark has a number. First find what each small mark is worth, then count from the number just before the needle.

Example

A scale has a number every 10 kg and 5 spaces between numbers. The needle is 3 marks past 20. What is the mass?

Each mark is 10 ÷ 5 = 2 kg. 3 marks are 6 kg. 20 + 6 = 26.

Answer: 26 kg

Read a container

Read the line at the top of the water. Use the same rule: find what each line is worth.

Solve word problems

All the amounts in a Grade 3 problem use the same unit. Decide what is happening, then add, subtract, multiply or divide. Write the unit in the answer.

StoryOperationAnswer
A 345 g book and a 278 g lunch box. Total mass?345 + 278623 g
A tub had 150 L. 60 L drained out. How much is left?150 − 6090 L
6 bags of flour, 2 kg each. Total mass?6 × 212 kg
24 L of juice shared equally into 4 jugs. Each jug?24 ÷ 46 L

On a pan balance, the lower pan is heavier. When the pans are level, both sides have the same mass.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting every mark as 1Check what one mark is worth: numbers ÷ spaces
Choosing grams for a heavy objectGrams for light things, kilograms for heavy things
Using grams or kilograms for water in a tubLiquid in a container is measured in liters
Thinking the higher pan is heavierThe heavier side goes down
Leaving out the unitWrite g, kg or L after the number

faq.q: What is the difference between grams and kilograms?
faq.a: Both measure mass. A gram is very light, about the mass of a paper clip. A kilogram is 1,000 grams, about the mass of a big dictionary, so it is used for heavier things.

faq.q: What are good benchmarks for 1 gram, 1 kilogram and 1 liter?
faq.a: A paper clip is about 1 gram, a big dictionary is about 1 kilogram, and a large water bottle holds about 1 liter. Children compare new objects with these to make estimates.

faq.q: How do you read a scale in 3rd grade math?
faq.a: Find two numbers next to each other and count the spaces between them. Divide to find what each mark is worth, then count the marks from the number just before the needle.

faq.q: Do 3rd graders convert between grams and kilograms?
faq.a: No. In standard 3.MD.A.2, word problems use the same unit throughout. Converting units, such as kilograms to grams, starts in Grade 4.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a key?
items.e: A key is small and light, so measure it in grams. Kilograms are for heavy things, and centimeters measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much water a kitchen sink holds?
items.e: The water in a sink is a liquid volume, so use liters. Grams and kilograms measure mass, and meters measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a slice of bread?
items.e: A slice of bread is light, so grams are the best unit. Kilograms are for heavy things, and centimeters measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a bag of potatoes?
items.e: A bag of potatoes is heavy, so kilograms are the best unit. Liters measure liquid, and meters measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much water a fish tank holds?
items.e: The water in a fish tank is a liquid volume, so use liters. Grams and kilograms measure mass, and meters measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring how much water a bathtub holds?
items.e: How much water a bathtub holds is a liquid volume. Liquid volume is measured in liters. Grams and kilograms measure mass, and meters measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a bicycle?
items.e: A bicycle is heavy. Heavy things are measured in kilograms. Liters measure liquid, and meters measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a strawberry?
items.e: A strawberry is very light, about as heavy as a few paper clips. Light things are measured in grams. Kilograms are for heavy things, and centimeters measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a pencil?
items.e: A pencil is light. You could hold many in one hand, so grams are the best unit. Kilograms are for heavy things, and centimeters measure length.

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a dog?
items.e: A dog is heavy, so measure its mass in kilograms. Liters measure liquid, and meters measure length.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a dictionary?
items.e: A big dictionary is the benchmark for 1 kilogram. 1 g is only a paper clip.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a bicycle?
items.e: A bicycle is about as heavy as 15 dictionaries, so about 15 kg. 15 g is as light as a few coins.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a paper clip?
items.e: A paper clip is the benchmark for 1 gram. 1 kg is as heavy as a dictionary.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the liquid volume of a bucket?
items.e: A bucket holds about 10 one-liter bottles of water, so about 10 L.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the liquid volume of a large milk jug?
items.e: A large milk jug holds about as much as 4 one-liter bottles, so about 4 L. Grams measure mass, not liquid.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the liquid volume of a full bathtub?
items.e: A bathtub holds a lot of water, about 150 L. 15 L is only a bucket and a half.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a pet cat?
items.e: A cat is about as heavy as 4 dictionaries, so about 4 kg. 40 kg is as heavy as a big dog.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a nickel?
items.e: A nickel has a mass of about 5 grams, about as much as 5 paper clips.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of an apple?
items.e: An apple is light but heavier than a paper clip. It is about 150 grams. 150 kg is heavier than a grown-up.

items.q: What is the best estimate for the mass of a watermelon?
items.e: A watermelon is about as heavy as 5 dictionaries, so about 5 kg.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which object is heavier?
items.e: The left side is lower. The lower pan holds the heavier object, so the watermelon is heavier and the orange is lighter.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which object is lighter?
items.e: The right side is lower. The lower pan holds the heavier object, so the bowling ball is heavier and the beach ball is lighter. A bigger object is not always heavier.

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the orange?
items.e: The pans are level, so the orange has the same mass as the weights: 100 + 50 + 50 = 200 g.

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the can of soup?
items.e: The pans are level, so the can of soup has the same mass as the weights: 200 + 200 = 400 g.

sets.title: Word problems with mass and volume

items.q: A fish tank has 22 L of water. Luis adds 17 L more. How much water is in the tank now?
items.e: Adding more means add: 22 + 17 = 39 L.

items.q: Lily has 30 kg of potatoes. She puts them into 5 sacks with the same mass. What is the mass of each sack?
items.e: Share 30 kg equally into 5 sacks: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 kg.

items.q: Grace buys 8 bottles of water for a picnic. Each bottle holds 2 L. How many liters of water does she buy?
items.e: 8 bottles of 2 L: 8 × 2 = 16 L.

items.q: Eli puts a book with a mass of 318 g and a pencil case with a mass of 125 g in his backpack. What is the total mass of the two things?
items.e: Put the masses together: 318 + 125 = 443 g.

items.q: A bathtub had 154 L of water. Then 68 L drained out. How much water is left in the bathtub?
items.e: Water went out, so subtract: 154 − 68 = 86 L.

items.q: A bag of dog food has 14 kg of food. Omar's dog eats 2 kg each week. How many weeks will the bag last?
items.e: How many groups of 2 kg are in 14 kg? 14 ÷ 2 = 7 weeks.

items.q: A box holds 4 toy cars that all have the same mass. Together the cars have a mass of 160 g. What is the mass of 1 toy car?
items.e: Share the mass equally: 160 ÷ 4 = 40 g.

items.q: Leo's watering can holds 7 L. He fills it 6 times to water the garden. How many liters of water does he use?
items.e: 6 times 7 L: 6 × 7 = 42 L.

items.q: A coach mixes 36 L of sports drink. The coach pours the same amount into 4 coolers. How many liters go into each cooler?
items.e: Share equally: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 L in each cooler.

items.q: Ruby's bicycle has a mass of 15 kg. Her scooter has a mass of 6 kg. How much heavier is the bicycle?
items.e: “How much heavier” compares two masses, so subtract: 15 − 6 = 9 kg.

items.q: A rain barrel had 46 L of water. A storm added 19 L. How much water is in the barrel now?
items.e: Add the water that came in: 46 + 19 = 65 L.

items.q: A baker uses 6 kg of flour each day. How many kilograms of flour does the baker use in 7 days?
items.e: 7 days of 6 kg: 7 × 6 = 42 kg.

items.q: A small wading pool holds 400 L when it is full. It has 263 L of water in it now. How many more liters are needed to fill it?
items.e: Find the missing part: 400 − 263 = 137 L.

items.q: A puppy had a mass of 6 kg in the spring. Now it has a mass of 15 kg. How many kilograms did it gain?
items.e: Find the difference: 15 − 6 = 9 kg.

items.q: A bucket holds 10 L. How many full buckets of water are needed to fill a tank that holds 80 L?
items.e: How many 10 L buckets make 80 L? 80 ÷ 10 = 8 buckets.

items.q: Noah's backpack full of books has a mass of 6 kg. The empty backpack has a mass of 2 kg. What is the mass of the books?
items.e: Take away the backpack: 6 − 2 = 4 kg.

items.q: A store has 7 bags of rice. Each bag has a mass of 4 kg. What is the total mass of the rice?
items.e: 7 equal bags of 4 kg: 7 × 4 = 28 kg.

items.q: One egg has a mass of about 50 g. What is the mass of 5 eggs?
items.e: 5 equal groups of 50 g: 5 × 50 = 250 g.

items.q: Jack picks 48 kg of apples. He packs them into 8 bags with the same mass. What is the mass of each bag?
items.e: Share equally: 48 ÷ 8 = 6 kg in each bag.

items.q: A bag had 860 g of flour. Emma used 383 g to bake bread. How much flour is left in the bag?
items.e: Flour was used up, so subtract: 860 − 383 = 477 g.
